fact: Guard rail: never touch a real Claude config directory (`~/.claude*`), not even to read credentials; code that reads, writes or swaps credentials is exercised only against temporary directories the test creates and removes (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:21).

Guard rail: never kill a process found by name, path or pattern; kill only a PID you spawned yourself (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:18). This binds developers' tests, not the product's own detection of external processes, which only reads /proc and never signals.

There is no end-to-end suite: each Gherkin acceptance criterion maps to a server integration test that drives the behaviour through the service or RPC boundary a client would use; a criterion only a real client can prove is named as unproven (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:48).

Tests are red first, Chicago School: real collaborators, doubles only at real boundaries (provider CLIs, network, clock, filesystem outside a temp dir); no sleeps, no polling — drain `OrchestrationEffectWorkerV2.drain` or await the persisted event or Deferred (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:29).

Unit tests are `*.test.ts` next to the source (Vitest); server integration tests are `*.integration.test.ts`, the orchestration testkit `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/testkit`, or `apps/server/integration`; one file runs with `node .loop-forge/test-scoped.mjs <path>` (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:44).
Contracts first: anything crossing the wire is typed in `packages/contracts`; a change there reaches server, web, mobile and desktop (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:85).
A ticket needing a new dependency, a new external service, or a change to `.loop-forge/` or `.github/` stops with `Human` (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:93).
The fork must stay upstreamable to `pingdotgg/t3code`: no fork-only conventions in product code (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:9).
The gate per ticket is `vp run --filter <pkg> typecheck`, `vp lint <files>`, `vp fmt <files>`; never `vp check` or repo-wide test/typecheck (.loop-forge/GUARDRAILS.md:62).

Server features are services; a `ws.ts` RPC handler, HTTP route or MCP tool decodes input, calls one service method and maps errors — filesystem, process, rollback logic belongs in the service (AGENTS.md:154, docs/internals/effect-services.md:9).

A service module is ordered imports, errors and schemas, the `Context.Service` tag with interface inline, `make`, then `layer`; tag ids look like `t3/area/Foo`; errors are `Schema.TaggedError` classes with a `message` getter (docs/internals/effect-services.md:38).

Effect modules are imported as namespaces from subpaths (`import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"`); consumers use `import * as Foo from "./Foo.ts"` then `Foo.Foo` / `Foo.layer`; no standalone `FooShape`, use `Foo["Service"]` (docs/internals/effect-services.md:69).

Dependencies come from the environment (`yield* FileSystem.FileSystem`), never as `make` parameters; Knip fails CI on an unused export, so `make` stays private unless imported (docs/internals/effect-services.md:77).

Reusable effect functions use `Effect.fn("Service.operation")` with a stable span name; `Effect.fnUntraced` only for per-event/tight-loop work with a nearby reason (AGENTS.md:156, docs/internals/effect-services.md:93).
Service tests exercise behaviour through the service, with test layers only for external dependencies; logic under test is never mocked (docs/internals/effect-services.md:90).

AGENTS.md "Hit every surface": a user-triggerable capability should also be reachable by agents through MCP tools and scheduled tasks, which works only when it is a service method, not handler code (AGENTS.md:72).
Comments say why (a constraint, an external quirk, an invariant), never restate names or narrate steps; lint rule `t3code/no-low-value-comments` catches mechanical cases (AGENTS.md:163).

Internal architecture constraints live in `docs/internals/`; provider account/process isolation constraints are in docs/internals/providers.md, which a change to Claude account handling may need to update (docs/internals/providers.md:12).

Docs rule: a driver kind identifies an integration; an instance identifies one configuration and account lifecycle; route work by instance so two accounts using the same driver do not share session state (docs/internals/providers.md:8).

Precedent: Antigravity sign-out closes admission to new processes and stops existing processes before clearing account metadata, otherwise a resumed session could retain the old account (docs/internals/providers.md:72).

A "Claude setup" maps to a Claude provider instance whose config dir is resolved by `resolveClaudeHomePath`: `homePath` setting if non-empty (with `~` expansion), else inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude` (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:12).

`makeClaudeEnvironment` sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to the resolved home only when `homePath` is configured; with an empty `homePath` the spawned CLI inherits the server env unchanged (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:30).

The Claude continuation group key is `claude:home:<resolved config dir>`, so two provider instances pointing at the same config dir share one continuation group and are effectively the same setup (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:67).

`claudeSignedOutMessage` is the existing user-facing text when Claude cannot authenticate: it tells the user to run `claude auth login` with the instance's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, then start a new thread (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:92).
`ClaudeHome.test.ts` uses `it.layer(NodeServices.layer)` from `@effect/vitest` with `it.effect` and resolves paths with `effect/Path` (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.test.ts:16).

On Linux the Claude CLI keeps its OAuth login in `<configDir>/.credentials.json` under `claudeAiOauth` (with `accessToken`); T3 already reads this file to call Anthropic's usage API, and skips it on darwin where the login is in the keychain (apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:20, apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:139).

The Claude account identity lives in `.claude.json` under `oauthAccount` (T3 reads `organizationUuid`); the file is `<configDir>/.claude.json` when a config dir is configured or inherited, else `~/.claude.json` in the home directory, not inside `~/.claude` (apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:23, apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:183).

`claudeAccountConfigPath(configDir | undefined)` returns the `.claude.json` path; ClaudeDriver passes the config dir only when `homePath` or inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:159).

`.claude.json` also holds the CLI's other settings, project history and MCP config, so a switch must replace only the `oauthAccount` key and leave every other key byte-for-byte intact; `.credentials.json` may hold logins for other services (e.g. `mcpOAuth`) besides `claudeAiOauth` (apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:20).

T3 already calls `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` with `authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`, `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` and a `claude-cli/<version>` user agent, 10 s timeout, failures swallowed to `undefined` (apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:146, apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:155).

The Claude provider snapshot's `auth.email` comes from the Claude Agent SDK initialization (`init.account.email`) of a capability probe that spawns the CLI, cached per instance on binary + resolved home (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:404, apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:199).

`claudeAuthStatus` treats a probe as unauthenticated only when `tokenSource` is `"none"` and no API key, email or subscription type is present; the probe resolves even for a logged-out CLI (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:170).

ClaudeDriver invalidates the capabilities probe cache when a status check reports unauthenticated; a cached probe otherwise lives for `CAPABILITIES_PROBE_TTL` when it carried fresh usage, so after an account switch the snapshot's email can lag unless the cache is invalidated (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:239, apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:276).

ClaudeDriver declares `supportsMultipleInstances: true`; `create` receives `instanceId`, `displayName`, `environment`, `enabled`, `config` (ClaudeSettings) and builds adapter, text generation and status check per instance (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:107).

The Claude driver provides no `auth` controller (no in-T3 sign-in), so `ProviderAuthService` operations on a Claude instance fail with "This provider does not support sign-in in T3 Code." (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderAuthService.ts:74).

`ProviderAuthService.stopSessions(instanceId, binding)` reads runtime recovery thread ids from the projection store, and releases every provider session of the instance whose status is not `stopped`/`error` via `ProviderSessionManagerV2.release({ reason: "manual_shutdown", detail: "Provider sign-in changed." })` (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderAuthService.ts:94).

`ProviderAuthService` serializes credential changes with a single `Semaphore.make(1)` (`credentialChanges`) wrapped around start, import and logout (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderAuthService.ts:72).
`stopSessions` is a private function inside `makeProviderAuthService`, not exported; reusing it from another service requires extracting it (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderAuthService.ts:94).

`ProviderSetupError({ instanceId, operation, detail })` from `@t3tools/contracts` is the existing typed error for provider credential operations, carrying a user-readable `detail` (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderAuthService.ts:80).

`ProviderAuthController` in provider-core defines optional `credentialBinding`, `adoptCredentials(update, stopSessions)`, `isChangingCredentials`, `invalidate`, `start`, `complete`, `logout` hooks (packages/provider-core/src/server/auth.ts:12).

Claude provider turns spawn the CLI through the Claude Agent SDK `query`; on non-Windows T3 wraps the native binary with `agentScope.wrap({ name: "claude", threadId })` and spawns it in its own process group via `spawnClaudeProcessGroup` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:901, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:922).

When systemd user scopes are available, T3 agent processes run in a scope under slice `app-t3code-agents-<sha256(stateDir)[0:12]>.slice` (`ownedAgentSlice`), while terminals that survive restart use `app-t3code-agents.slice` (apps/server/src/process/agentScope.ts:21, apps/server/src/process/agentScope.ts:331).

A systemd-run scope's process is not a descendant of the T3 server in the process tree; without systemd the agent is a plain child process of the server, so "started by T3" detection needs both the owned agent slice in `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` and the server's process ancestry (apps/server/src/process/agentScope.ts:315, packages/shared/src/AgentScope.ts:75).

Existing /proc scanning precedent: `PortDiscovery` lists `/proc`, filters numeric entries, reads `/proc/<pid>/fd` links and `/proc/<pid>/comm`, swallowing per-process read errors with `Effect.orElseSucceed`, and only on `hostPlatform === "linux"` (apps/server/src/preview/PortScanner.ts:399, apps/server/src/preview/PortScanner.ts:432).
`apps/server/src/cli/update.ts` reads `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` to classify a process (apps/server/src/cli/update.ts:277).

Platform is read via `HostProcess.Platform` (a `Context.Reference<NodeJS.Platform>` from `@t3tools/shared/HostProcess`), which tests can override; `HomeDirectory`, `Environment`, `UserId` are references in the same module (packages/shared/src/HostProcess.ts:7).

`writeFileStringAtomically({ filePath, contents })` in `@t3tools/shared/atomicWrite` writes to a temp file in the target directory and renames over the target (resolving symlinks first), so a single-file write is atomic on Linux (packages/shared/src/atomicWrite.ts:29).
`@t3tools/shared/KeyedLock` provides `make<Key>()` returning `withLock(key, effect)` and `activeKeys`; it is not reentrant (packages/shared/src/KeyedLock.ts:5).

The capability probe, text generation and status checks also spawn the Claude CLI with the instance's environment, as children of the server, at any time (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:360, apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:192).

Persistence migrations are numbered `NNN_Name.ts` under apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations; the latest is `066_RepairClientSettlementTimestamps.ts` (apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/066_RepairClientSettlementTimestamps.ts:1).

The Claude adapter passes MCP servers over the CLI's stdin control channel instead of argv because argv is readable by every local user, and logs only server names because error texts can echo headers — an existing precedent for keeping credentials out of argv and logs (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:892).

T3's secret store is the service `ServerSecretStore` (tag `t3/auth/ServerSecretStore`) with `get(name)` → `Option<Uint8Array>`, `set(name, value)`, `create(name, value)`, `getOrCreateRandom(name, bytes)`, `remove(name)` and an optional `directory` (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:138).
Secrets live in `<stateDir>/secrets`, where `stateDir` is `<baseDir>/userdata` (or `<baseDir>/dev` in dev) (apps/server/src/config.ts:120).
On start the secret store creates its directory recursively and chmods it to `0o700`; a failed chmod raises `SecretStoreSecureError` (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:160).

Each secret is one file `<name>.bin` in the secrets directory; there is no encryption, keyring or OS keychain on the server side — protection is file permissions only (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:171).

`ServerSecretStore.set` writes `<path>.<uuid>.tmp`, chmods it `0o600`, renames it into place and chmods `0o600` again; on failure it deletes the temp file and raises `SecretStorePersistError` (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:189).
`ServerSecretStore.create` opens with flag `wx` and mode `0o600`, so an existing file is a failure (`isSecretAlreadyExistsError`) (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:226).
`ServerSecretStore.get` returns `Option.none` for a missing file and `SecretStoreReadError` otherwise; `remove` treats a missing file as success (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:173).

`SecretStoreError` is a union of nine tagged errors (Secure, Read, TemporaryPath, Persist, RandomGeneration, ConcurrentRead, Remove, Decode, Encode), each with `resource` (e.g. `secret <name>`) and `cause` (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:19).

`ProviderCredentialStore.make(driver, bindingId)` hashes `${driver.length}:${driver}${bindingId}` with SHA-256 into the secret name `provider-auth-<hex>` "so arbitrary bindings cannot escape or exceed a filename", returning `{ binding: { owner: "t3", key }, get, set, remove }` over `ServerSecretStore` (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderCredentialStore.ts:6).

Drivers reach credentials through `ProviderHost.credentials(namespace, bindingId)`, which maps errors to `ProviderCredentialError({ operation: "get" | "set" | "remove" })` with message "Could not <op> stored provider credentials." (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderHostLive.ts:39, packages/provider-core/src/server/errors.ts:18).

The only user of `ProviderCredentialStore` today is Codex ChatGPT OAuth, which stores its tokens as JSON bytes under namespaces `codex-chatgpt` and `codex-chatgpt-registration` keyed by instance id (apps/server/src/provider/CodexChatGptAuth.ts:157).
Codex serialises credential changes with a per-binding semaphore plus `withChatGptSessionLock(secrets.directory, binding.key, …)` (apps/server/src/provider/CodexChatGptAuth.ts:162).

Settings secrets are named `provider-config-<b64url(instanceId)>-<b64url(driver)>-<b64url(field)>` and `provider-env-<b64url(instanceId)>-<b64url(name)>` in the secret store (apps/server/src/settingsSecrets.ts:79).

The redacted-secret placeholder for clients is `SECRET_REDACTED = "••••••"`, and `redactServerSettingsForClient` blanks every sensitive settings value before settings reach a client (apps/server/src/settingsSecrets.ts:23, apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts:131).

`moveInlineSettingsSecrets` moves plaintext secret fields out of `settings.json` into the secret store and logs only "failed to move a settings secret into the secret store", never the value (apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts:625).

`SecretRequests` (tag `t3/secrets/SecretRequests`) is another secret-store client whose design rule is that a value "never reaches the transcript, projections, clients, or model context" (apps/server/src/secrets/SecretRequests.ts:1).

`SecretRequests` lists `store.directory` to sweep expired entries hourly — the only existing pattern for enumerating secrets, since `ServerSecretStore` has no list method (apps/server/src/secrets/SecretRequests.ts:223).

Tests double `ServerSecretStore` either by building `ServerSecretStore.ServerSecretStore.of({...})` inline or with an in-memory `layerMemorySecretStore` (`Layer.sync` over a `Map<string, Uint8Array>`) that exists only inside a test file; no exported reusable memory layer exists (apps/server/src/mcp/OrchestratorMcpToolkit.integration.test.ts:505, apps/server/src/provider/ProviderCredentialStore.test.ts:11).
`ServerSecretStore.test.ts` asserts permissions by spying on `chmod` (one `0o700` on the directory, at least two `0o600`) (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.test.ts:190).
The triage CLI prompt tells agents "Secrets dir (NEVER read this)" (apps/server/src/cli/triagePrompt.ts:220).
Cloud link credentials (relay credentials, link key pair) also live in `ServerSecretStore` under fixed names (apps/server/src/cloud/CliState.ts:46).

The Claude server checks auth with `claude --version` (20 s timeout) followed by an Agent SDK `query()` capability probe that never yields a prompt and reads `init.account`; there is no `claude auth status` call anywhere (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:516, apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:349).

A signed-out Claude instance reports `auth: { status: "unauthenticated" }` with "Claude Code is not authenticated. Run `claude auth login` and try again."; a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` skips the check (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:627).
A signed-in Claude status carries `email`, `workspaceId` and a type/label such as "Claude Max Subscription", "Claude API Key", "Amazon Bedrock" (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:652).

The capability probe has a 25 s timeout and disables hooks, filesystem MCP servers and claude.ai MCP (`ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS: "false"`), discarding stderr (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:196).
`ClaudeSettings.homePath` is titled "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR path" with description "Keeps .claude.json and .claude separate." (packages/contracts/src/settings.ts:660).

`claudeUsageLimits.ts` reads no files or tokens, it only maps the SDK `get_usage` response; `Drivers/claudeUsage.ts` reads only transcripts under `<config dir>/projects` (apps/server/src/provider/claudeUsageLimits.ts:1, apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/claudeUsage.ts:96).

`claudeResetCredits.ts` is the only Claude credential reader: it decodes `.credentials.json` as `claudeAiOauth.accessToken` only and `.claude.json` as `oauthAccount.organizationUuid` only, reading a missing file as `{}` (apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:125).

Nothing in apps/server or packages reads `refreshToken`, `expiresAt` or `emailAddress` from a Claude file today; the only `refreshToken`/`accessToken` fields belong to `ChatGptTransferredProfile.credentials` (packages/contracts/src/providerSetup.ts:216).

`claudeResetCredits.test.ts` pins the darwin skip by providing `HostProcess.Platform` = `"darwin"`, the existing pattern for platform-gated tests (apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.test.ts:124).

T3 calls `api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` and `/api/organizations/<org>/reset_rate_limits` with the Claude bearer token; failure texts are fixed strings like "Claude could not read its login." (apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:56).
`ProviderSetupError`'s comment states its rule: "Safe setup failure text. Never include OAuth codes, URLs, or native token data." (packages/contracts/src/providerSetup.ts:187).

`serverLogger.ts` does no key-based redaction; the code relies on `effect/Redacted` (e.g. `Redacted.make(token)`) and on logging only error tags or lengths, never payloads (apps/server/src/serverLogger.ts:32, apps/server/src/device/ExpoApi.ts:78).

`EventNdjsonLogger.ts` has no redaction logic; Codex protocol logging redacts keys ending in `authorization`, `apikey`, `token`, `password`, `secret` and `Bearer …` strings (apps/server/src/provider/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:207, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/CodexAdapterV2.ts:1485).

`redactProviderFailureText` strips URL credentials, `Bearer`/`Basic` values, `access_token`/`api_key`/`token`/`secret` pairs and `sk-…` keys from provider failure text (packages/provider-core/src/server/failure.ts:145).
Existing logs record only `errorTag` or lengths, e.g. "Claude capability probe failed." `{ errorTag }` (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:427).

"Unavailable on this platform" has no shared form: it appears as `failure: "unsupported-platform"`, as an `unsupportedPlatform` code with a message, and Claude reset credits quietly return `undefined` on darwin (apps/server/src/cloud/ManagedEndpointRuntime.ts:29, packages/contracts/src/browserImport.ts:26).

Server auth policy is `desktop-managed-local`, `loopback-browser`, `remote-reachable` or `unsafe-no-auth`; sessions use browser cookie, bearer or DPoP tokens (packages/contracts/src/auth.ts:12, apps/server/src/auth/EnvironmentAuthPolicy.ts:23).

Every WS method must declare a scope in `RPC_REQUIRED_SCOPES` (compile- and run-time enforced); all `provider.auth.*` RPCs require `providers:manage` (apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:40, apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:211).

The provider auth RPCs are `provider.auth.start`, `.complete`, `.respond`, `.cancel`, `.logout`, `.subscribe`; `ProviderAuthState` exposes `credentialOwner: "provider" | "t3"` (packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:411, packages/contracts/src/providerSetup.ts:118).
Only the desktop app uses an OS keyring (Electron `safeStorage`); the server has none (apps/desktop/src/settings/DesktopSavedEnvironments.ts:229).

The Claude driver kind is `claudeAgent` (`ProviderDriverKind.make("claudeAgent")`), and the default instance id of a driver is its driver kind, so the default Claude setup's instance id is `claudeAgent` (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:66, packages/contracts/src/providerInstance.ts:92).

`ProviderInstanceConfig` is `{ driver, displayName?, accentColor?, environment?, enabled?, config?: unknown }`; ClaudeDriver decodes `config` with `Schema.decodeSync(ClaudeSettings)` (packages/contracts/src/providerInstance.ts:55, apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:64).

`deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap(settings)` is the exported function that turns `ServerSettings` into the effective instance map, adding the default instance of each built-in driver that has none and enabling project-overridden instances (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:36).

`mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment(environment)` overlays an instance's configured environment variables on `process.env`, expanding `~` in `CODEX_HOME` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` values (packages/provider-core/src/server/instanceEnvironment.ts:7).

`ProviderInstanceRegistry` (tag `t3/provider/ProviderInstanceRegistry`) exposes `getInstance(id)`, `listInstances`, `listUnavailable`, `streamChanges`, `subscribeChanges`; a `ProviderInstance` exposes `instanceId`, `driverKind`, `continuationIdentity`, `snapshot`, `invalidateCaches`, `orchestrationAdapter`, `textGeneration`, optional `auth` — but not its config dir (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderInstanceRegistry.ts:24, packages/provider-core/src/server/driver.ts:42).

The Claude `ProviderInstance.invalidateCaches` is `Cache.invalidateAll(capabilitiesProbeCache)`, the hook to make the snapshot re-probe the logged-in account (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:398).

The Claude instance's `continuationIdentity.continuationKey` is the continuation group key `claude:home:<dir>`; it loses whether the dir was explicit or the default, so it cannot locate `.claude.json` on its own (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:392).

ClaudeDriver computes `configDir = resolveClaudeHomePath(config, processEnv)` and `accountConfigPath = claudeAccountConfigPath(homePath || CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ? configDir : undefined)` inline in `create`; no shared helper returns both paths (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:158).

`ResetCreditCoordinator` (tag `t3/provider/resetCreditCoordinator`) is a server-level service in `ClaudeDriverEnv` that serialises account-level actions on the Claude config directory, because instances sharing a directory share the login (apps/server/src/provider/resetCreditCoordinator.ts:1, apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:336).

Adding a service to `ClaudeDriverEnv` ripples into every harness that builds drivers: `ResetCreditCoordinator.layerTest` is provided at six places in ProviderRegistry.test.ts alone (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderRegistry.test.ts:3504).

Server-wide services are composed in `apps/server/src/server.ts`, e.g. `ResetCreditCoordinator.layer`, `ProviderLatestVersions.layer` in `layerRuntimeCoreDependencies`, with `ServerSecretStore.layer` provided below them (apps/server/src/server.ts:635, apps/server/src/server.ts:658).

`ServerSettingsService` (getSettings, updateSettings, streamChanges) has `layerTest(overrides: DeepPartial<ServerSettings>)`, which deep-merges overrides into defaults, so a test can declare Claude instances with temp `homePath`s (apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts:179, apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts:260).
`ServerSecretStore.layer` is `Layer.effect(ServerSecretStore, make)`; it needs `ServerConfig` for the secrets dir (apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.ts:316).

WS method names live in the `WS_METHODS` constant with dotted provider names, e.g. `providerConsumeResetCredit: "provider.consumeResetCredit"`, `providerAuthLogout: "provider.auth.logout"` (packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:380).

Each RPC is `Rpc.make(WS_METHODS.x, { payload, success, error })` named `Ws<Name>Rpc`, listed in `WsRpcGroup = RpcGroup.make(...)` which ends with `.middleware(RpcScopeAuthorization)` (packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:629, packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:1882).

A new WS method needs an entry in `RPC_REQUIRED_SCOPES` (`satisfies Record<WsRpcMethod, AuthEnvironmentScope>`, provider methods use `AuthProvidersManageScope`) and an instrumentation category in RpcInstrumentation, both compile-time checked (apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts:63, apps/server/src/observability/RpcInstrumentation.ts:215).

Provider setup RPC errors are `ProviderSetupRpcError = Schema.Union([ProviderSetupError, EnvironmentAuthorizationError])`; the standard payload is `ProviderSetupInput = { instanceId: ProviderInstanceId }` (packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:627, packages/contracts/src/providerSetup.ts:12).

WS handlers are built in `layerWsRpc` via `ServerWsRpcGroup.of({ [METHOD]: (input) => ... })`; the provider auth handlers are one-line delegations like `providerAuth.logout(input)` (apps/server/src/ws.ts:1806, apps/server/src/ws.ts:2343).

ws.test.ts tests RPCs in-process with `RpcServer.makeNoSerialization` over `layerWsRpc(...)`; no integration test drives provider handlers end to end, tests call services directly (apps/server/src/ws.test.ts:602).
Client mutations use `createEnvironmentRpcCommand({ tag, concurrency })` in client-runtime, e.g. reset credits (packages/client-runtime/src/state/server.ts:1146).

ACP precedent for "stop live sessions, then change config": `providerSessionManager.closeInstance(instanceId)`, then `setProvider`, then `providerRegistry.refreshInstance(instanceId)` (apps/server/src/ws.ts:1601).

Instance config changes go through `server.updateSettings` with `providerInstanceMutation`, handled by `serverSettings.updateProviderInstance(...)`; when an entry changes, `ProviderInstanceRegistry.reconcile` closes the old instance scope and calls `driver.create` again (apps/server/src/ws.ts:2385, apps/server/src/provider/ProviderInstanceRegistry.ts:180).
`ClaudeSettings` has `enabled`, `binaryPath` (default `"claude"`), `homePath` (default `""`), `customModels`, `launchArgs`, `autoCompactWindow` (packages/contracts/src/settings.ts:646).

A thread binds to a provider instance through `providerInstanceId` on `OrchestrationV2AppThread`; runs, attempts, provider sessions and provider threads each carry `providerInstanceId` too (packages/contracts/src/orchestrationV2.ts:377, packages/contracts/src/orchestrationV2.ts:759).

The interrupt command is `{ type: "run.interrupt", commandId, threadId, runId, reason?, holdQueue? }`; the thread-wide variant is `thread.stop`; both are routed in the orchestrator (packages/contracts/src/orchestrationV2.ts:2862, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Orchestrator.ts:479).

Run and attempt status literals include `interrupted` separately from `failed` and `cancelled`; provider session status is `starting | ready | running | waiting | stopped | error` (packages/contracts/src/orchestrationV2.ts:452, packages/contracts/src/orchestrationV2.ts:760).

`dispatchRunInterrupt` writes a `run_interrupt_request` turn item; with no started provider turn it sets attempt, node and run to `interrupted` at once, with no live session it calls `settleInterruptedRun`, otherwise it enqueues a `provider-turn.interrupt` outbox effect (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Orchestrator.ts:9467).

The effect worker runs `provider-turn.interrupt` via `providerTurnControl.interrupt` and then dispatches `thread.background-work.settle`; "is not active" style failures are swallowed as non-retryable (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EffectWorker.ts:157, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EffectWorker.ts:47).

`ProviderTurnControlService.interrupt` calls `session.interruptTurn({ providerThread, providerTurnId, requestRuntimeRestart: true })` and waits up to 2 s for the turn to leave `running`; `interruptAndAwaitTerminal` waits up to 1000 runtime yields and fails if the turn does not terminalize (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderTurnControlService.ts:182, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderTurnControlService.ts:257).

An adapter's interrupted terminal becomes attempt/run status `interrupted`, and `makeInterruptResultTurnItem` builds the "Interrupted" item (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/RunExecutionService.ts:634).

Releasing a provider session mid-turn FAILS the run: `releaseEntry` calls `failSubscribers` unless the reason is `server_shutdown`, and `RunExecutionService` then writes a failed terminal (`status: "failed"`); so `ProviderAuthService.stopSessions` and `closeInstance` end a running turn as failed, not stopped (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:1020, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/RunExecutionService.ts:866).
Release with `server_shutdown` interrupts subscribers instead and leaves the run to restart recovery (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:549).

`ProviderSessionManagerV2` (`ProviderSessionManagerV2Shape`) offers `open`, `get`, `isLive`, `close`, `closeInstance(instanceId)`, `release({ providerSessionId, reason, detail? })`, `detach`, `shutdown`; release reasons are `idle_timeout | runtime_error | manual_shutdown | server_shutdown` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:145, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:65).

`closeInstance(instanceId)` releases every live session whose `entry.runtime.instanceId` matches with `manual_shutdown` and detail "Provider instance X logged out."; it is tested at ProviderSessionManager.test.ts:903 (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:2317).

After a release the session projection becomes `stopped` (`error` only for `runtime_error`) and pending live runtime requests become `cancelled` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:235).

Active sessions of an instance are found from projections with `projections.getRecoveryThreadIds("runtime")` then `getThreadRecords(threadId, ["providerSessions"])`, filtering on `providerInstanceId` and status not stopped/error (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProjectionStore.ts:555, apps/server/src/provider/ProviderAuthService.ts:112).

`ThreadManagementService.interruptThread` finds the thread's `latestActiveRun` and dispatches `run.interrupt`; `ThreadManagementService.dispatch` is the server-side command API (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ThreadManagementService.ts:985, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ThreadManagementService.ts:323).

On the next turn `ProviderTurnStartService` calls `providerSessions.open({ providerSessionId, resumeFromSession, initialNativeThreadId })`, and `open` fetches the adapter for the instance from the registry at that moment (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderTurnStartService.ts:541, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:2141).

Claude resume: `makeClaudeQueryOptions` sets `{ resume: nativeThreadId }` when resuming, and `shouldResume` is true when the session was opened with resume or has a persisted provider turn, so a freshly opened session on an existing thread resumes the same Claude conversation (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:1243, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:9137).

Claude conversation transcripts are under `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/...`; a switch that keeps the config dir keeps the continuation key and the transcripts, so resume keeps working, whereas a `homePath` change makes `decideProviderSessionTransition` choose `create_with_handoff` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionTransitionPolicy.ts:46, apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/claudeUsage.ts:96).

`ProviderContinuationService` is not about Claude session resume: it dispatches background-task completion wakes with `queue_after_active` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderContinuationService.ts:53).

Restart continuation precedent: `prepareForShutdown` enqueues `provider-runtime.continue` effects and `continueRestartedRun` dispatches `message.dispatch` with `restartContinuationOfRunId` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts:755, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/RestartContinuation.ts:189).

`runOrchestratorV2Scenario` runs scripted steps (`dispatch`, `await_run_status`, `await_thread_idle`, …) against `OrchestratorV2` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/testkit/OrchestratorScenario.ts:30).

`ProviderReplayHarness.layerWithRegistry(scenario, registryLayer, { runEffectWorker?, … })` builds the full in-memory runtime (memory SQLite, stores, ProviderSessionManager, EffectWorker); it mocks `ProviderAuthService` with only `tryHandlePromptCommand` and has no real `ProviderInstanceRegistry`, tests inject a `ProviderAdapterRegistryV2` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/testkit/ProviderReplayHarness.ts:257, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/testkit/ProviderReplayHarness.ts:400).

`OrchestrationEffectWorkerV2.drain(maxEffects?)` loops `runOnce()` until nothing is claimable; with `runEffectWorker: false` the harness does not fork the daemon (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EffectWorker.ts:820, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/testkit/ProviderReplayHarness.ts:519).

Fake adapters register via `ProviderAdapterRegistry.layerSingle(adapter)` / `layerFromAdapters`; a hand-written fake adapter with `openSession`, `events: Stream.fromQueue`, `startTurn`, `interruptTurn` is in BackgroundWorkStop.integration.test.ts (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderAdapterRegistry.ts:180, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/BackgroundWorkStop.integration.test.ts:58).

Interrupt test pattern: `orchestrator.dispatch({ type: "run.interrupt", … })`, `worker.drain()`, then assert runs, attempts and turn items are `interrupted` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/BackgroundWorkStop.integration.test.ts:906).

Account-switch precedent test "resumes a queued account switch without requiring a portable handoff": two instances share a continuation key, and the test asserts the same `nativeThreadRef` and zero `contextHandoffs` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/testkit/ProviderSwitch.integration.test.ts:1825).

`ClaudeOrchestratorReplayHarness` lives in ClaudeAdapterV2.testkit.ts with fixtures such as `claude_idle_resume`, `provider_thread_resume` under testkit/fixtures (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.testkit.ts:2875).

`apps/server/integration/` holds only transfer-budget and SQL measurement tests; orchestration integration tests are `*.integration.test.ts` under `src/orchestration-v2` (apps/server/integration/transferBudgetV2.integration.test.ts:1).

`createClaudeAdapterV2` fixes the merged environment (`makeClaudeEnvironment`) at adapter creation and passes it per query as `env` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:10325, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:1346).

`ServerConfig.layerTest(cwd, { prefix })` creates a temp base dir for tests; ServerSecretStore.test.ts builds `Layer.provide(ServerSecretStore.layer, ServerConfig.layerTest(process.cwd(), { prefix: "t3-secret-store-test-" }))` — a real secret store over a temp dir (apps/server/src/config.ts:232, apps/server/src/auth/ServerSecretStore.test.ts:15).
The server derives `stateDir` as `<baseDir>/userdata` (or `<baseDir>/dev` with a dev URL) and the database as `<stateDir>/statev2.sqlite` (apps/server/src/config.ts:120).
`claudeAccountConfigPath` has exactly one importer, ClaudeDriver (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:159).

No Claude account switching, remembering or login copying exists anywhere in the repository today; Claude has no `ProviderAuthController`, so the `provider.auth.*` RPCs do not apply to it (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:387).

`writeFileStringAtomically` creates its temp file with `fs.writeFileString` and no mode, so the replaced file gets the default mode (0666 minus umask, typically 0644) instead of keeping the target's mode; it is unsuitable for `.credentials.json`, which must stay 0600 (packages/shared/src/atomicWrite.ts:47).

`makeClaudeEnvironment` is called at five sites: ClaudeProvider probe and workspace snapshot, ClaudeTextGeneration, ClaudeAdapterV2 adapter creation, and terminal/Manager.ts, so terminals the user opens in T3 also get the Claude environment of a setup (apps/server/src/terminal/Manager.ts:1463, apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:441, apps/server/src/textGeneration/ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:93, apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:10338).

`probeClaudeCapabilities(claudeSettings, environment?, cwd?, includeUsage = true)` is exported; it spawns the CLI via the Agent SDK with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` from `makeClaudeEnvironment`, and with `includeUsage` asks the CLI for `usage_EXPERIMENTAL_MAY_CHANGE_DO_NOT_RELY_ON_THIS_API_YET({ skipBehaviors: true })` under its own timeout, returning `usage` only when that request succeeded — the one existing path where the CLI itself talks to Anthropic with its stored login (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:349, apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:390, apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:748).

The Claude CLI version is known only from `checkClaudeProviderStatus`'s `claude --version` run; `readClaudeResetCredits(configDir, version)` takes it as a parameter for the `claude-cli/<version>` user agent, and `API_BASE` and `withClaudeHeaders` are private to claudeResetCredits.ts (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:516, apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts:14).
`ownedAgentSlice(stateDir)` is an exported function of agentScope.ts (apps/server/src/process/agentScope.ts:23).

`makeClaudeEnvironment(config, baseEnv?)` returns `baseEnv ?? process.env` itself (same object) when `homePath` is empty, and a spread copy with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` otherwise; ClaudeHome.test.ts:26 pins the identity with `toBe(process.env)` (apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts:30).

ClaudeProvider.ts:441 is `runClaudeCommand`, which spawns `claude <args>` (e.g. `--version`) through `ChildProcess.make` with the `makeClaudeEnvironment` result; ClaudeProvider.ts:357 is the capability probe's environment (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeProvider.ts:435).

Terminal/Manager.ts calls `makeClaudeEnvironment(config.value, resolved)` inside `resolveProviderInstanceTerminalEnvironment` for `claudeAgent` instances, so terminals get the setup's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (apps/server/src/terminal/Manager.ts:1460).

Spawn-env seams: ProviderRegistry.test.ts records `runClaudeCommand` spawns and asserts `recorded.commands.map((c) => c.env?.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR)` (apps/server/src/provider/ProviderRegistry.test.ts:4539); ClaudeCapabilitiesProbe.test.ts asserts the probe query's `options.env` (apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeCapabilitiesProbe.test.ts:113).
ClaudeAdapterV2.test.ts provides a `ClaudeAgentSdkQueryRunner` double whose `open(input)` records `input.options.env` (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.test.ts:1424).

ClaudeTextGeneration.test.ts puts a fake `claude` (ClaudeTextGeneration.fixture.mjs) on PATH and drives it with `T3_FAKE_CLAUDE_*` env; the fixture fails with exit 5 when `T3_FAKE_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR_MUST_BE` differs from its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (apps/server/src/textGeneration/testing/ClaudeTextGeneration.fixture.mjs:61).

Manager.test.ts tests `TerminalManager.resolveProviderInstanceTerminalEnvironment({ serverSettings, path, rawProviderInstanceId: "claudeAgent", env })` and asserts on the returned `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (apps/server/src/terminal/Manager.test.ts:3003).

`agentScope.wrap` runs the command through `systemd-run --user --scope`, which execs the command in the caller's environment, so environment variables set on a T3 Claude spawn reach the CLI process inside the agent scope (apps/server/src/process/agentScope.ts:162).

`@t3tools/shared/HostProcess` has no process-id reference today; its references are Platform, Architecture, Hostname, Username, HomeDirectory, Environment, WorkingDirectory, ExecutablePath, Arguments, InvokedAs, IsExecutable, Addresses, UserId (packages/shared/src/HostProcess.ts:7).
